To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have successfully transplanted cryopreserved autologous peripheral blood stem cells (PBSCs) into a patient with multiple myeloma, 21 years after the cells were cryopreserved.

the use of autologous stem cells for transplantation in a patient with a rare disease after a 21 year period of cryopreservation is feasible and that the procedure is safe, with a low risk of complications.
cryopreserved autologous stem cells can be successfully rethawed and reinfused in the treatment of a patient with multiple sclerosis after 21 years.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of cryopreserved stem cells.
the development and application of the method of the cryoimmunological diagnostics.
the development of a new method to determine the temperature dependence of the diffusion coefficient of a solute in a solvent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cryopreservation of stem cells in a patient who has undergone autologous stem- cell transplantation for treatment of a malignant disease is not recommended.
the use of cryopreserved cells in autologous HSCT is safe and feasible.
, based on our case and the literature, the use of cryopreserved cells is safe and effective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that autologous cryopreserved stem cells can be used for successful transplantation in a patient who had a malignant melanoma and a severe graft-versus-host disease after an allogeneic stem-cell transplant.
we were able to perform a successful autologous stem- cell transplantation after cryopreservation of the stem cells in a patient with a severe autoimmune disease.
we have shown that it is feasible to use cryopreserved stem cells in the treatment of a patient with a hematological disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cryopreservation process does not affect the viability of the stem cells and that the cells can be used after 21 years.
it is feasible to cryopreserve and subsequently successfully thaw and transplant stem cells after 21 years, which is longer than any other published case.
cryopreserved cells are not a lost cause, and that they should be stored for as long as possible.
